name: Helion Energy
tagline: Pulsed-magnetic fusion, selling power to Microsoft
what: Fusion using a pulsed non-ignition approach that recovers electricity directly from the plasma rather than boiling water for a turbine. It holds the sector's only real commercial commitment: supplying a Central Washington data centre for Microsoft by 2028.
why: The most aggressive timeline in fusion by a wide margin, and the clearest example of the pattern running through this board — the man building the largest AI lab personally chairs the company trying to power it.
other_backers: Lightspeed, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Lux Capital, Peak XV, Nucor, Good Ventures (Dustin Moskovitz), Bill Ford

name: Commonwealth Fusion
tagline: SPARC tokamak, roughly three-quarters built
what: The best-capitalised fusion company in the world at roughly $3B raised. Its SPARC tokamak uses high-temperature superconducting magnets to shrink the reactor, and is around 75% complete.
why: The institutional counterweight to Helion — slower, more conventional physics, targeting the early 2030s. If fusion works, one of these two approaches will have been right.
other_backers: Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Google, Temasek, Eni

name: Pacific Fusion
tagline: Inertial confinement, funded in milestone tranches
what: Pulsed inertial-confinement fusion, funded through roughly $1B structured as milestone-based tranches rather than a single cheque.
why: The financing structure is the innovation. Tranching a billion dollars against physics milestones is how deep-tech capital gets disciplined, and other hard-science sectors are copying it.
other_backers: General Catalyst, Felicis, Mubadala

name: Valar Atomics
tagline: Factory-built fission reactors for AI datacentres
what: Small modular reactors designed to be mass-manufactured rather than built on site. Its NOVA Core prototype reached zero-power criticality at Los Alamos in November 2025 — the first under the DOE's Nuclear Reactor Pilot Programme — and has since powered an NVIDIA AI chip.
why: Tripled its valuation in four months on a working demonstration. Founded by a 27-year-old, backed by the Anduril founder, and pointed at the fact that every announced AI-nuclear deal depends on reactors that do not yet exist at scale.
other_backers: Sequoia (reported lead), Shyam Sankar, Riot Ventures

name: TerraPower
tagline: Sodium-cooled Natrium reactor plus storage
what: Advanced sodium-cooled reactor paired with gigawatt-scale molten-salt thermal storage, letting output follow demand instead of running flat.
why: Picked up $650M this summer with NVIDIA's venture arm joining — the chip company buying insurance on the power supply for its own customers.
other_backers: NVentures, SK Group, Bill Gates

name: Fervo Energy
tagline: Enhanced geothermal using shale drilling methods
what: Applies horizontal drilling and fracturing techniques from shale to geothermal, making hot rock viable in places conventional geothermal cannot reach. Contracted to supply data-centre load.
why: The only firm baseload clean power on this board that works with today's technology and today's supply chain. Unsexy, and the most likely of these to actually deliver electrons this decade.
other_backers: Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Devon Energy, Galvanize, Capricorn

name: Base Power
tagline: Home batteries assembled into a virtual power plant
what: Installs residential battery systems cheaply and aggregates them into a dispatchable grid resource, selling capacity back to the utility rather than selling hardware to the homeowner.
why: The distributed counter-position to everything else in this theme. Instead of building one enormous new plant, it assembles a plant out of houses that already exist.
other_backers: a16z, Thrive Capital, Valor Equity, Addition, Terrain

name: Oklo
tagline: Altman chaired it from Y Combinator to the NYSE
what: Compact fast-fission reactors sold as power rather than hardware, with the Aurora powerhouse design. Altman backed it out of Y Combinator, served as board chairman, and took it public in May 2024 through his own SPAC, AltC Acquisition Corp. He stepped down as chair in April 2025 explicitly to remove the conflict blocking supply deals between Oklo and OpenAI.
why: The company that proves the point about roles. On capital alone Oklo barely registers here; on involvement it was a decade-long chairmanship by the person who went on to run the largest AI lab. And the resignation is signal too — he gave up the seat so the company could sell power to his other company.
other_backers: Public markets; DCVC, Caisson Capital pre-listing

name: Exowatt
tagline: Modular solar-thermal power for datacentres
what: Shipping-container modules that capture solar energy as heat, store it for up to 24 hours, and dispatch electricity on demand — aimed specifically at powering data centres.
why: The unglamorous half of Altman's energy book. Fusion is the moonshot; this is the thing that could plausibly plug in this decade.
other_backers: Atomic, Felicis, a16z

name: Anthropic
tagline: World's most valuable private company
what: Frontier model lab behind Claude, valued at $965B as of July 2026 and holding the highest implied valuation on secondary markets of any private company. Confidential IPO paperwork is filed.
why: It overtook OpenAI on private-market pricing — the first time the challenger has out-valued the incumbent — and did so on enterprise revenue rather than consumer reach.
other_backers: Google, Amazon, Lightspeed, ICONIQ, Fidelity

name: OpenAI
tagline: The incumbent, now second by valuation
what: Valued at $852B as of July 2026, with confidential IPO paperwork filed and the $500B Stargate compute build-out underway.
why: Read it as a hub, not a node. It leads the round in Altman's brain-interface company, partners with his longevity company, and its Startup Fund sits on cap tables across this board.
other_backers: Microsoft, SoftBank, MGX, Thrive, Sequoia

name: DeepSeek
tagline: Open weights, AGI-only, founder-controlled
what: Raised $7.4B in June 2026 at north of $50B — its first ever external round — and is reportedly seeking fresh capital as high as $71B, with a China IPO signalled for 2027. Liang Wenfeng personally put in about $2.95B to remain the largest holder.
why: The governance is the story. Outside investors received virtually no voting rights, no board seats and a five-year lock-up. Nobody in the West raised money on those terms, and its founder is now wealthier than any Western AI creator.
other_backers: High-Flyer, state funds at provincial and municipal level

name: Moonshot AI
tagline: Kimi — China's fastest AI revenue ramp
what: Raised $2B at $20B in May 2026 on surging demand for open-source models, and is in talks at up to $30B — a third round in six months. ARR passed $200M in April, roughly doubling from $100M in early March.
why: A seven-fold repricing in six months on real revenue, not narrative. Together with DeepSeek, Zhipu and MiniMax it forms a Chinese front rank seeking over $180B combined.
other_backers: Alibaba, Tencent, HongShan, state-backed investors

name: Safe Superintelligence
tagline: No product, no revenue, $7B raised
what: Founded by OpenAI's former chief scientist with a single stated goal — build superintelligence with safety as the design constraint — and no product roadmap, no revenue and no published research.
why: Thirty-two billion dollars of pure reputation pricing. Whether you think that is rational is a fairly precise test of what you believe about this market.
other_backers: Greenoaks, a16z, Sequoia, Alphabet

name: Thinking Machines Lab
tagline: Mira Murati's lab
what: Founded by OpenAI's former CTO. Closed a $12B seed in July 2025 — one of the largest in history — and a $5B Series B in March 2026 at $50B.
why: Along with SSI, it prices the thesis that frontier capability walks out of the door with the people, not the org chart.
other_backers: a16z, Accel, ServiceNow Ventures, Cisco

name: Mistral AI
tagline: Europe's frontier lab
what: The leading European model lab at roughly $15B after a $1.5B Series C, positioned on open weights and data sovereignty.
why: The only serious Western non-US entrant. Its valuation is a rough market price on whether sovereignty is a real moat or a procurement preference.
other_backers: ASML, DST Global, General Catalyst, Lightspeed, Xavier Niel

name: AMI Labs
tagline: Yann LeCun's post-LLM lab
what: Founded in November 2025 by Meta's former chief AI scientist to build world models — systems that understand physical reality — on the explicit argument that language models are a dead end for real intelligence.
why: A billion dollars at seed to bet against the entire prevailing architecture, co-led by Bezos. The most senior contrarian position on the board.
other_backers: Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro Capital, HV Capital

name: 01.AI
tagline: Kai-Fu Lee's lab, heading for Hong Kong
what: Kai-Fu Lee's model company, raising ahead of a Hong Kong listing targeted for 2027 after pivoting from frontier training toward enterprise deployment.
why: The cautionary entry in China's front rank — it stepped back from the most expensive training runs and repositioned on applications. A live read on how many labs one country can actually sustain.
other_backers: Sinovation Ventures, Alibaba Cloud, HongShan

name: Reflection AI
tagline: Open frontier models, ex-DeepMind founders
what: Founded by former DeepMind researchers to build open-weight frontier models as a Western answer to the Chinese labs, positioned around autonomous coding and agents.
why: The US response to DeepSeek's open-weight strategy, and the only place Alexandr Wang has put personal money outside his own companies.
other_backers: Sequoia, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, DST Global

name: Physical Intelligence
tagline: One general policy for any robot
what: Building a single general-purpose control model that runs on any robot body rather than training each machine per task. Confirmed at $5.6B in November 2025 and reported in talks above $11B.
why: The purest software-layer bet in robotics, and the one the smart money keeps re-upping on. Bezos, Thrive and Lux have followed on through every round.
other_backers: CapitalG, Lux Capital, Index, T. Rowe Price, Amazon, OpenAI

name: Figure AI
tagline: Humanoids for commercial work
what: General-purpose humanoid robots aimed at logistics and manufacturing, at $39B post-money after raising over $1B.
why: The highest-valued humanoid company in the world, and the one where the gap between valuation and deployed fleet is widest. A genuine test of whether this theme is early or overpriced.
other_backers: Parkway Venture Capital, Microsoft, OpenAI Startup Fund, Brookfield, Intel Capital, Qualcomm, Salesforce, LG

name: Unitree Robotics
tagline: Shipping humanoids at volume, listing in Shanghai
what: Cleared the Shanghai Stock Exchange listing committee in June 2026 as the first embodied-AI company approved for China's A-share market, targeting roughly $6.2B and a $616M raise. Aims to deliver 10,000–20,000 humanoid units worldwide in 2026.
why: The single most uncomfortable data point on this board. Western humanoid companies are valued at five times Unitree while shipping a fraction of the units — Chinese makers accounted for roughly 85–90% of global humanoid shipments in 2025.
other_backers: Hangzhou state innovation funds, Meituan, Tencent, Alibaba, China Mobile
caveat: IPO floor ~¥42bn from prospectus filings, not company PR. STAR Market subscription 10 Aug 2026. Revenue ¥1.699bn, net profit ¥590m (2025).

name: AgiBot (Zhiyuan)
tagline: 10,000 units delivered in under three years
what: Hit its 10,000th cumulative humanoid delivery in March 2026, less than three years after founding, and is pursuing a listing by taking control of an already-listed company rather than a direct IPO.
why: Along with Unitree it forms a genuine production duopoly. The backdoor listing route is a reminder that Chinese robotics is solving for capital-markets access on a completely different path.
other_backers: Hillhouse, BYD, Tencent, HongShan, state funds
caveat: HK$40–50bn is pre-marketing guidance, not a closed round. Aggregator totals for capital raised are irreconcilable. Also took control of A-share listed Shangwei New Materials as a backdoor vehicle.

name: Galbot
tagline: China's highest-valued unlisted humanoid company
what: Announced a ¥2.5B financing round in March 2026, making it the most valuable Chinese humanoid company still private, with retail-store deployments running in Beijing.
why: Backed by an operating company — Meituan — rather than pure financial investors, which is how most of China's robotics capital is actually structured.
other_backers: Meituan, CATL, HongShan, Beijing state funds
caveat: ¥2.5bn round Mar 2026 well sourced; the >¥20bn valuation is investor-sourced. National AI Industry Investment Fund and Bank of China on the cap table.

name: Skild AI
tagline: A shared brain across robot types
what: A general robot foundation model trained to transfer across radically different bodies — quadrupeds, arms, humanoids — from a single policy. Raised close to $1.4B in January 2026.
why: Went from research spin-out to $14B in under two years. The speed is the signal: investors are racing to own the control layer before it consolidates.
other_backers: SoftBank, Lightspeed, Samsung, Sequoia, Coatue

name: Apptronik
tagline: Apollo humanoid, with Mercedes and Google
what: Maker of the Apollo humanoid, with over $935M in a serially extended Series A after a $520M extension in February 2026.
why: The hardware-first counter-position to Skild and Physical Intelligence, with real industrial pilots at Mercedes-Benz and GXO rather than demo videos.
other_backers: Google, Mercedes-Benz, B Capital, Capital Factory

name: 1X Technologies
tagline: NEO, the humanoid for the home
what: The only major humanoid company targeting domestic use first, with its NEO robot pitched at household tasks. Reported to be seeking $1B at over $10B.
why: Everyone else is chasing warehouses because the economics are legible. Going after the home first is either the biggest market on the board or a category error.
other_backers: OpenAI Startup Fund, EQT Ventures, Samsung NEXT, Nistad

name: Agility Robotics
tagline: Digit, already working paid shifts
what: Maker of Digit, a bipedal warehouse robot working commercial shifts for GXO and Schaeffler. Raised roughly $400M.
why: The least speculative company in the theme — actual robots doing actual paid work — and correspondingly the lowest valuation. The market is not paying for deployment; it is paying for generality.
other_backers: WP Global Partners, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, DCVC

name: Anduril Industries
tagline: Software-defined defence prime
what: Autonomous defence systems built as a product company rather than a cost-plus contractor — surveillance towers, loitering munitions, counter-drone, and the Lattice software beneath them. $5B Series H at $61B in May 2026, reportedly in talks at $100B.
why: The most densely co-invested company on this entire board. If any single company represents the consensus of this group, it is this one.
other_backers: Valor Equity, Fidelity, Founders Fund, Sands Capital

name: Palantir
tagline: The origin story of this entire theme
what: Thiel launched it in 2003 and has chaired the board ever since — a twenty-three-year commitment, by far the longest on this board. Joe Lonsdale co-founded it. Trae Stephens was an early employee before co-founding Anduril, and Shyam Sankar, its chief technology officer, backs Valar Atomics.
why: Included despite being listed because the involvement graph explains everything else. Nearly every defence and national-capability position here traces back through Palantir alumni. Remove this node and the cluster looks like coincidence; include it and it looks like a lineage.
other_backers: Public markets since 2020 direct listing

name: Helsing
tagline: Europe's defence AI champion
what: AI software and autonomous systems for European militaries, from strike drones to submarine sensing. Raised $1.8B at $18B in July 2026 — the largest defence-tech round Europe has produced — and remains roughly 80% European-owned.
why: Daniel Ek seeded it with €100M through Prima Materia and chairs the board. It is the single clearest instance of a consumer-tech founder deliberately building strategic sovereignty rather than returns.
other_backers: Prima Materia, Accel, Greenoaks, General Catalyst, Saab

name: Shield AI
tagline: Autonomy stack for aircraft
what: Hivemind, an autonomy stack that flies aircraft without GPS, comms or a pilot, plus the V-BAT drone it runs on. Raised $2B in March 2026.
why: Sells the autonomy software into existing airframes as well as its own — a licensing wedge into primes that will never buy a whole Anduril stack.
other_backers: a16z American Dynamism, Riot Ventures, US Innovative Technology Fund, Airbus Ventures

name: Saronic
tagline: Autonomous surface vessels
what: Unmanned naval vessels built at speed and volume, on the argument that a distributed fleet of cheap autonomous boats beats a small number of exquisite ships. $1.75B Series D in March 2026.
why: Grew faster in valuation than any other defence company on the board this year, and is the clearest expression of the mass-over-exquisite doctrine the sector is arguing for.
other_backers: 8VC, General Catalyst, Caffeinated Capital, a16z

name: Castelion
tagline: Low-cost hypersonic strike
what: Founded by SpaceX veterans to apply mass-manufacturing methods to hypersonic strike weapons, with an explicit goal of an order-of-magnitude cost reduction against legacy munitions.
why: Tests whether the SpaceX playbook transfers to munitions. If it does, the entire defence cost structure is in play.
other_backers: 8VC, Lightspeed, First In, a16z

name: Hermeus
tagline: Hypersonic aircraft
what: Reusable hypersonic aircraft, progressing through a deliberate sequence of increasingly capable flight-test vehicles rather than attempting the final design first.
why: One of the few places where the defence thesis and the commercial-aviation thesis genuinely overlap — the same airframe argument serves both.
other_backers: Founders Fund, Sam Altman, In-Q-Tel, Canaan

name: Retro Biosciences
tagline: Ten more years of healthy life
what: Founded on a $180M personal cheque from Altman with the stated mission of adding ten years to healthy human lifespan. Its first drug, RTR242, targets Alzheimer's by boosting autophagy and is in human trials. A partnership with OpenAI produced a model that made cell reprogramming roughly fifty times more efficient.
why: The cleanest demonstration of the whole thesis on this board: the AI lab's models directly accelerating the founder's biology company. Now raising $1B at a reported $5B.
other_backers: Sequoia (reported), Kleiner Perkins

name: Altos Labs
tagline: Cellular rejuvenation, $3B+ raised
what: The best-funded longevity company ever created, at over $3B raised, pursuing partial epigenetic reprogramming to restore cells to a younger state without losing their identity.
why: Hired Nobel laureates at pharma-beating salaries and then went quiet. Five years in, it is the benchmark the rest of the field is implicitly measured against.
other_backers: ARCH Venture Partners, Yuri Milner, Bob Nelson

name: NewLimit
tagline: Armstrong's epigenetic reprogramming bet
what: Co-founded by Coinbase's chief executive to reprogram the epigenome of aged cells. Raised $435M at $3.1B in June 2026 and says it has a prototype therapy that reverses the age of some human cells. First human trial planned for 2027, in liver disease.
why: Went $130M → $45M → $435M in about thirteen months, which is what repeated technical validation looks like from outside. Founders Fund led, with Thrive and NFDG following.
other_backers: Kleiner Perkins, Greenoaks, Eli Lilly Ventures, Human Capital, Dimension

name: Manas AI
tagline: Hoffman's AI drug discovery company
what: Co-founded by Reid Hoffman with the oncologist and author Siddhartha Mukherjee to compress drug discovery using AI-generated chemical libraries, starting with cancer targets.
why: Small by capital, large by signal — Hoffman left the Microsoft board in June 2026 to run it. When a career investor goes operator, that is a conviction statement money cannot express.
other_backers: General Catalyst, Greylock

name: Lila Sciences
tagline: Fully automated AI science factories
what: Builds 'AI Science Factories' — closed-loop laboratories where agents generate hypotheses, design protocols, drive lab robots, capture the data and retrain overnight. $550M raised at over $1.3B, now reportedly in talks at $8.5B with NVIDIA joining.
why: A six-fold repricing inside a year on the proposition that the scientific method itself can be run as a compute workload. If any theme on this board reprices violently in the next eighteen months, this is the candidate.
other_backers: Flagship Pioneering, NVIDIA, General Catalyst

name: Periodic Labs
tagline: Automating materials discovery
what: Founded in 2025 by a ChatGPT co-creator and a DeepMind research scientist to automate materials design end to end. Raised $300M in an a16z-led seed and is in talks at roughly $7B.
why: A seed-stage company discussing a seven-billion-dollar valuation. Materials is the bottleneck under batteries, chips, reactors and aircraft — solve discovery there and most other themes on this board move.
other_backers: a16z, Accel, Bain Capital, Felicis, NVIDIA, Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt (reported)

name: Isomorphic Labs
tagline: DeepMind's drug design company
what: Spun out of DeepMind to apply AlphaFold-lineage models to drug design, with pharma partnerships at Eli Lilly and Novartis and its first internal candidates advancing.
why: The most credentialed entry in the theme and the only one run by someone who has already won a Nobel for the underlying science.
other_backers: Alphabet, Thrive Capital, GV

name: Arc Institute
tagline: Science funding outside the grant system
what: A non-profit institute co-founded by Patrick Collison that funds scientists on eight-year unrestricted terms rather than per-project grants, and has produced significant work in genome editing and biological foundation models.
why: Not an investment and has no valuation — which is the point. It is a bet that the bottleneck on biology is the funding mechanism itself, not the science.
other_backers: Silvana Konermann, Patrick Hsu, philanthropic funding

name: Extropic
tagline: Thermodynamic sampling units
what: Building an entirely new class of semiconductor that uses the natural thermodynamic noise of ordinary CMOS transistors to sample directly from probability distributions, rather than computing them deterministically. Signed a letter of intent with the US Department of Commerce in July 2026 for up to $75M through the CHIPS R&D office.
why: The single earliest genuinely-new-physics bet on this board. A government willing to underwrite onshore manufacturing for a chip category that does not yet have a product is an unusually strong pre-commercial signal.
other_backers: Kindred Ventures, Buckley Ventures, US Dept of Commerce (LOI)

name: Normal Computing
tagline: Thermodynamic ASICs and chip verification
what: Pairs physics-based thermodynamic ASICs promising order-of-magnitude energy reductions with an AI electronic-design-automation product that pays the bills today. Raised $50M in strategic funding led by Samsung Catalyst.
why: The commercially sober version of the same physics. Selling design tools now while the exotic silicon matures is how this category survives long enough to matter.
other_backers: Samsung Catalyst, Celesta, First Spark, Micron Ventures

name: PsiQuantum
tagline: Photonic fault-tolerant quantum computing
what: Building a million-qubit photonic quantum computer using standard semiconductor fabrication, skipping the intermediate noisy-device generation entirely. Closed $1.5B in May 2026 at $10.5B.
why: The largest private quantum bet in the world, and the only one attempting utility-scale fault tolerance directly. Its scale makes the rest of this theme look like a rounding error.
other_backers: BlackRock, Temasek, Baillie Gifford, NVentures, Microsoft

name: SandboxAQ
tagline: Schmidt's AI-plus-quantum Alphabet spinout
what: Spun out of Alphabet in March 2022 with Jack Hidary as chief executive and Eric Schmidt as chairman, a role he has held since. Applies large quantitative models and post-quantum cryptography across biopharma, chemicals, navigation and financial services. Around $950M raised at roughly $5.75B.
why: Schmidt chairs this while simultaneously running Relativity Space — two of the deepest time commitments any operator on this board has made, and neither of them is where his money is largest. Worth noting the company is contesting serious governance litigation brought by a former chief of staff.
other_backers: T. Rowe Price, Breyer Capital, Guggenheim Partners, TIME Ventures, Thomas Tull

name: Rain AI
tagline: Analog in-memory compute
what: Brain-inspired analog chips that perform computation inside memory rather than shuttling data to a separate processor, targeting the energy wall rather than the throughput wall.
why: Altman was an early backer years before the energy constraint became the sector's defining problem. The thesis has aged into relevance.
other_backers: Prosperity7, Grep VC, Airbus Ventures

name: Crusoe
tagline: Builds the power plant and the datacentre
what: Vertically integrated AI infrastructure — generates the power and builds the data centre around it. It constructed the Abilene, Texas campus for OpenAI's Stargate programme, now operational. Revenue went from $276M in 2024 to roughly $998M in 2025.
why: Tripled its valuation in eight months, the fastest climb of any AI infrastructure company this year. The physical answer to where the electricity comes from.
other_backers: Valor Equity, Mubadala, Fidelity, Founders Fund, NVIDIA, Tiger Global, Lowercarbon

name: Etched
tagline: A chip that only runs transformers
what: Burns the transformer architecture directly into silicon, trading all generality for enormous throughput on the one architecture that matters. Raised $500M at $5B in early 2026.
why: The highest-variance bet in silicon. If the transformer stays dominant it wins outright; if the world-model labs on this board are right about architecture, the premise expires.
other_backers: Stripes, Two Sigma, Primary Venture Partners, Positive Sum

name: MatX
tagline: Ex-Google TPU team, chips for large models
what: Founded by former Google TPU engineers to build silicon optimised specifically for very large language models rather than general acceleration. $500M Series B in February 2026.
why: One of Patrick Collison's small number of personal positions, and Karpathy's most recent. When the people who understand the workload best both buy the same chip company, that is the signal.
other_backers: Jane Street, Situational Awareness, Homebrew, Nat Friedman

name: Unconventional AI
tagline: Brain-inspired analog silicon
what: Analog, brain-inspired computing rather than digital matrix multiplication. Raised $475M in a single seed round — roughly 110 times the median AI-chip seed.
why: A seed round that size is not a seed round; it is a bet placed before anyone can evaluate it. Bezos backing it says the physics case was convincing enough to skip the usual proof.
other_backers: Undisclosed

name: Nscale
tagline: Europe's sovereign AI hyperscaler
what: Vertically integrated sovereign AI infrastructure — GPU capacity, networking and orchestration, built on cheap Nordic hydro power. Raised $2B in March 2026 at $14.6B, the largest Series C in European history.
why: The infrastructure expression of the same sovereignty thesis Mistral and Helsing trade on, and the largest private company in Europe by valuation on this board. Aker and 8090 Industries co-led with NVIDIA, Dell, Nokia, Lenovo, Citadel, Point72 and Jane Street participating.
other_backers: Aker ASA, 8090 Industries, NVIDIA, Dell, Nokia, Lenovo, Citadel, Point72, Jane Street, Astra Capital

name: Project Prometheus
tagline: An artificial general engineer
what: Co-led by Jeff Bezos himself. Building AI that does the intellectual work of engineering — designing, testing and helping manufacture physical objects across chips, jet engines, batteries and pharmaceuticals. Bezos describes it as a very modern version of CAD, and insists it has nothing to do with robotics. Raised $12B at ~$41B in June 2026.
why: The largest new company on this board and the boldest single thesis: that the next model compresses the timeline from invention to manufactured product. Bezos came out of investor retirement to run it.
other_backers: Undisclosed institutional syndicate, >$18B total funding

name: World Labs
tagline: Fei-Fei Li's spatial intelligence lab
what: Founded by the researcher behind ImageNet to build large world models with spatial intelligence — systems that generate and reason about persistent 3D environments. $1B round in February 2026 at $5.4B.
why: The most academically credentialed entry in the theme, and its round drew Autodesk, AMD and NVIDIA together — three companies whose businesses only converge if this thesis is right.
other_backers: Autodesk, AMD, Fidelity, Radical Ventures

name: Decart
tagline: Real-time generative world simulation
what: Real-time interactive world generation — video environments produced and steered live rather than rendered in advance. Raised $300M at over $4B.
why: The only company here shipping consumer-facing world models today. It is the theme's proof that the technology works before the industrial applications arrive.
other_backers: NVIDIA, Sequoia, Benchmark, eBay Ventures, Adobe Ventures, Toyota Ventures

name: General Intuition
tagline: Spatial reasoning learned from game video
what: Trains agents on a vast corpus of gameplay video to learn spatial and temporal reasoning, on the argument that games are the cheapest available simulation of embodied cause and effect. $320M at $2.3B in June 2026.
why: Khosla and Bezos Expeditions in the same round is the world-model thesis meeting the physical-AI thesis — two of the most active operators arriving at the same place from opposite directions.
other_backers: General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures

name: Odyssey
tagline: Interactive video world models
what: World models for interactive video and simulation, raising $310M at $1.45B in June 2026 with Amazon, AMD and Google's venture arm participating.
why: Signed to AWS Trainium rather than NVIDIA — one of the first visible places where the world-model boom is being used to contest the silicon monopoly underneath it.
other_backers: Amazon, AMD, GV, EQT Ventures, Pioneer Fund

name: Stripe
tagline: The payments layer under the AI economy
what: Internet payments infrastructure, valued at $159B in a February 2026 tender offer. Its founders have repeatedly said they are in no hurry to list.
why: The quiet giant of this board. Altman holds roughly $633M of it, Thrive's largest single position is here, and it remains the default financial substrate for most of the software companies listed above.
other_backers: Sequoia, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, GIC

name: Erebor
tagline: A chartered bank for the tech economy
what: A digital bank founded by Palmer Luckey that received a US national bank charter in February 2026 — the first granted under the current administration. It lends against crypto and private securities, finances AI chips, and serves startups traditional banks won't underwrite. Reported to be raising at $8B or more.
why: Founders Fund, a16z, Lux and 8VC on one cap table, formed directly in the vacuum left by Silicon Valley Bank. The ecosystem decided to own its own bank rather than lobby one.
other_backers: Founders Fund, a16z, Lux Capital, 8VC, Haun Ventures

name: Tools for Humanity (World)
tagline: Proof of human, chaired by Altman
what: Founded in 2019 by Alex Blania as chief executive with Sam Altman as chairman. Builds the Orb, an iris scanner issuing a World ID intended to prove a person is human rather than an AI agent. Around $240M raised at roughly $2.5B, 33 million app users and 15 million Orb-verified, with US partners including Tinder, Zoom and Docusign.
why: Altman's most direct hedge against his own product: if agents flood the internet, proof of personhood becomes infrastructure. It is also the honest counter-example on this board — it reportedly cut staff in June 2026 struggling to convert users into revenue. A chairmanship is not a guarantee.
other_backers: a16z, Bain Capital Crypto, Khosla Ventures, Blockchain Capital

name: Kalshi
tagline: CFTC-regulated event exchange
what: A federally regulated US exchange for trading on real-world events. Raised over $1B at $22B led by Coatue, and is seeking roughly $40B — double that — with an IPO floated for no earlier than 2027.
why: Doubled its valuation twice inside a year by taking the regulated path its rival avoided. Regulation turned out to be the moat, not the tax.
other_backers: Coatue, Sequoia, Paradigm, a16z crypto

name: Ramp
tagline: Corporate spend, now agent-driven
what: Corporate cards and spend management at $44B, increasingly positioned around agents that execute finance operations rather than dashboards that display them.
why: Founders Fund has followed on through every round. The least exotic company on this board and one of the fastest revenue compounders on it.
other_backers: Founders Fund, Thrive, General Catalyst, Khosla, Sequoia

name: Polymarket
tagline: The crypto-native prediction market
what: Blockchain-settled prediction markets, seeking $400M at $15B. The Intercontinental Exchange — owner of the NYSE — has committed $2B in total.
why: Thiel led its round when it was worth about $1B. That the operator of the New York Stock Exchange has since put two billion dollars in is the clearest institutional validation any theme here has received.
other_backers: Intercontinental Exchange, Founders Fund, Blockchain Capital, 1confirmation

name: Neuralink
tagline: Implanted electrodes, nine patients
what: A surgically implanted brain-computer interface placed by removing a section of skull, with roughly $1.85B raised and nine human volunteers implanted as of early 2026.
why: With SpaceX public and xAI folded into it, this is now most of Musk's remaining private surface area. It is also the only company in this theme with a meaningful patient cohort.
other_backers: Founders Fund, Vy Capital, Sequoia, Thrive

name: Merge Labs
tagline: Interface without surgery
what: Co-founded by Sam Altman to reach neurons without opening the skull — using ultrasound and engineered molecular interfaces rather than electrodes. Emerged from stealth in January 2026 with $252M at $850M, in a round led by OpenAI itself.
why: OpenAI leading a round in its own chief executive's company is the most direct conflict-of-interest structure on this board, and the most explicit statement of where he thinks the human-AI relationship ends up.
other_backers: OpenAI, Bain Capital, Gabe Newell

name: Synchron
tagline: Implant delivered through a blood vessel
what: Places its Stentrode electrode array through a blood vessel via catheter, avoiding open brain surgery entirely. $200M Series D in November 2025, running a 2026 pivotal trial aimed at becoming the first FDA-approved BCI.
why: The regulatory front-runner. If the first approved brain-computer interface arrives by catheter rather than craniotomy, the surgical approach loses years of market access.
other_backers: ARCH Venture Partners, Bezos Expeditions, Gates Frontier, Khosla Ventures

name: Precision Neuroscience
tagline: Film that rests on the brain surface
what: A thin-film electrode array that sits on the cortical surface without penetrating tissue, and is reversible. Progressing through FDA clearances.
why: The third distinct physical bet in this theme — penetrate, catheterise, or lay on top. The theme is not converging on an approach, which is what early actually looks like.
other_backers: Steadview Capital, Forepont, B Capital, Duquesne Family Office

name: Neko Health
tagline: Whole-body scanning for healthy people
what: Co-founded by Daniel Ek in 2023. Full-body sensor scans that screen asymptomatic people for early disease markers in minutes, raising $700M at $7B in 2026 from a €30M seed.
why: A 200x mark-up in three years on a consumer health product with waiting lists across Europe. It is the commercial front end of the same thesis the longevity labs are pursuing biologically.
other_backers: Prima Materia, Lightspeed, General Catalyst, Atomico

name: Function Health
tagline: Continuous blood biomarker testing
what: Subscription lab testing that measures a hundred-plus biomarkers twice a year and interprets them, bypassing the primary-care gatekeeper entirely. Acquired a full-body MRI company to add imaging.
why: The American analogue to Neko, built on labs rather than scanners. Both are wagers that people will pay out of pocket for data their healthcare system declines to collect.
other_backers: a16z, Andreessen Horowitz Bio, Redpoint, K5

name: Oura
tagline: The wearable that got taken seriously
what: Finnish smart-ring maker measuring sleep, temperature and cardiovascular metrics continuously, now used clinically and reportedly valued around $11B after a 2026 round.
why: The only company in this theme with a decade of longitudinal consumer data, which is exactly the asset the AI-for-health thesis requires and cannot buy.
other_backers: Fidelity, Dexcom, Forerunner, Temasek

name: Relativity Space
tagline: 3D-printed rockets, Schmidt in the chair
what: Largely 3D-printed launch vehicles, with the Terran R medium-lift rocket and a growing commercial backlog. Eric Schmidt took over as chief executive and chairman in 2025 and is pushing the company toward data centres in orbit.
why: A former Google chief executive left investing to personally run a rocket company so it could put AI compute in space. Either the most interesting sentence on this board or the most telling one.
other_backers: Eric Schmidt (majority), Fidelity, BlackRock, Tiger Global

name: Impulse Space
tagline: Getting things to the right orbit
what: In-space transportation — the tugs and kick stages that move payloads from where a rocket drops them to where they actually need to be. $500M Series D at $4.26B.
why: Launch is nearly solved and getting cheap. The bottleneck has moved to last-mile orbital logistics, and Founders Fund got there first.
other_backers: Founders Fund, Lux Capital, RTX Ventures, DCVC

name: Aetherflux
tagline: Beaming solar power down from orbit
what: Founded by a Robinhood co-founder to collect solar energy in low Earth orbit and beam it to small ground receivers by infrared laser, with a first demonstration satellite planned for 2026. In talks at $2B on about $80M raised to date.
why: A twenty-five-fold step-up on a company that has not yet flown. Space solar has been a physics-paper idea for fifty years — this is the first time a credible founder has put personal capital and a launch date against it.
other_backers: Index Ventures, Interlagos, Breakthrough Energy, a16z, NEA

name: Varda Space
tagline: Pharmaceutical manufacturing in orbit
what: Manufactures pharmaceutical crystals in microgravity and returns them to Earth in a re-entry capsule, exploiting the fact that some molecules form structures in orbit they cannot form under gravity.
why: The first company treating orbit as a factory floor with a returning product rather than a service in the sky. It has flown and recovered capsules already.
other_backers: Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, 8VC

name: Stoke Space
tagline: Fully and rapidly reusable rockets
what: Building Nova, designed for full reusability of both stages including a novel actively cooled second-stage heat shield. $350M Series D-II in February 2026.
why: Full second-stage reuse is the one thing even SpaceX has not achieved. Solving it resets launch economics again.
other_backers: Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Y Combinator, Point72, Industrious Ventures

name: K2 Space
tagline: Big satellites at small-satellite prices
what: Very large, very cheap satellites designed for the new generation of high-capacity launchers, inverting the industry's decade-long march toward miniaturisation.
why: Cheap heavy lift changes the optimal satellite design. K2 is the clearest bet that the smallsat era was a constraint artefact, not an endpoint.
other_backers: Altimeter, Lightspeed, First Round, Alpine Space Ventures

name: Waymo
tagline: The autonomy business that actually works
what: Fully driverless commercial ride-hailing across a growing set of US cities, raising $16B at $126B in February 2026 — nearly triple its October 2024 mark.
why: The valuation nearly tripled in fifteen months on deployment, not promise. It is the reference price for every other autonomy company on this board.
other_backers: Alphabet, Silver Lake, a16z, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price

name: Waabi
tagline: Simulation-first autonomy, now with Uber
what: Trains its driver almost entirely in simulation rather than on public roads. Raised up to $1B in January 2026 — $750M immediate, $250M milestone-linked to Uber — and pivoted from trucking toward a multi-modal stack targeting 25,000 robotaxis on Uber.
why: The pivot is the story. Waabi's founder spent years arguing trucking was the right first market; the capital has now bought a redirection into robotaxis.
other_backers: Uber, Khosla Ventures, NVIDIA, Porsche Automobil Holding

name: Nuro
tagline: Licensing the driver to everyone else
what: Abandoned its own delivery robots to license its autonomy stack to carmakers and ride-hail platforms. $203M Series E at $6B, with NVIDIA and Uber joining.
why: The most instructive failure-and-recovery on the board: it stopped competing on hardware and became a supplier, and the market immediately re-rated it upward.
other_backers: NVIDIA, Uber, Baillie Gifford, Icehouse, Kindred Ventures

name: Wayve
tagline: End-to-end driving from raw video
what: End-to-end learned driving with no HD maps and no hand-written rules — a single model from camera input to control output, licensed to carmakers rather than run as a fleet.
why: The European entry, and the purest expression of the foundation-model approach to driving. NVIDIA is on the cap table for the same reason it is on most of this board.
other_backers: SoftBank, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Uber

name: XPeng AeroHT
tagline: Modular flying car, in volume production
what: XPeng's eVTOL affiliate, building a road-and-air modular vehicle with a dedicated mass-production plant in Guangzhou — the first flying-car factory built for volume rather than prototypes.
why: He Xiaopeng runs cars, humanoids and aircraft off one engineering base on the argument that they are the same robotics problem. Nobody in the West is attempting that spread.
other_backers: XPeng, IDG Capital, Sequoia China, Guangzhou state funds

name: Slate Auto
tagline: A deliberately basic electric pickup
what: A stripped-down, modular, sub-$30,000 electric pickup with no paint options and no touchscreen, designed for owner customisation after purchase.
why: The contrarian position in mobility — while everyone else adds autonomy, Bezos is funding the removal of features to reach a price point nobody else serves.
other_backers: Bezos Expeditions, General Catalyst, TWG Global

name: Anysphere (Cursor)
tagline: The fastest revenue ramp in software
what: The AI coding environment Cursor, at roughly $2B ARR on a $29.3B priced Series D. In April 2026 SpaceX paid $10B for exclusive collaboration rights plus an option to acquire the company outright at $60B.
why: That option is the most unusual structure on this board — a rocket company buying a call on a code editor. It prices the belief that whoever owns the developer surface owns the deployment of everything else.
other_backers: Accel, Coatue, Thrive, a16z, Benchmark

name: Perplexity
tagline: Answers instead of links
what: AI-native search returning cited answers rather than a page of links, at around 20 million monthly users and expanding into an agentic browser.
why: The most widely co-held company among individual operators on this board — Bezos, Friedman and Gross, Naval and Lütke all hold it personally. Direct, unhedged bets against Google search.
other_backers: IVP, NEA, SoftBank Vision Fund, Bezos Expeditions

name: Harvey
tagline: AI for the legal profession
what: Domain-specific AI for law firms and in-house legal teams, deployed across a large share of the top global firms.
why: The template every vertical AI company is now copying: pick a profession with high billing rates and low tolerance for error, and sell to the firm rather than the individual.
other_backers: Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, OpenAI Startup Fund, GV, Coatue

name: Sierra
tagline: Agents that handle customers, priced on outcomes
what: Bret Taylor's company building customer-facing AI agents that resolve issues end to end, charging per resolution rather than per seat. Raised $950M at $15.8B in May 2026, with over $150M ARR and more than 40% of the Fortune 50 as customers.
why: Taylor runs this as chief executive while chairing OpenAI's board — the most concentrated governance position on the entire board, and one that puts him on both sides of the agent layer at once.
other_backers: Sequoia, Benchmark, Thrive, ICONIQ, Greenoaks

name: XBOW
tagline: AI that attacks your systems first
what: Autonomous offensive security — AI that finds exploitable vulnerabilities the way an attacker would, and reached the top of HackerOne's US leaderboard doing it.
why: Friedman and Gross followed on into the Series C in March 2026. Their re-ups have historically been a better indicator than their entries.
other_backers: Sequoia, Altimeter, NFDG

name: Promptfoo
tagline: Testing and securing AI applications
what: Open-source evaluation and red-teaming for AI applications — the test harness for systems whose outputs are not deterministic.
why: Lütke's most recent position, and a bet on the unglamorous layer that has to exist before AI applications ship into regulated environments.
other_backers: Insight Partners, a16z

name: KoBold Metals
tagline: AI-guided critical mineral exploration
what: Uses machine learning over geological data to find copper, lithium and nickel deposits conventional surveying misses. Raised $537M at $2.96B and is committing $600M into Zambia by end of 2026 — the largest private American investment there since independence.
why: Everything else on this board is downstream of minerals nobody can currently find fast enough. Gates and Bezos both backing the same exploration company is the most fundamental supply-side bet here.
other_backers: Breakthrough Energy Ventures, a16z, Equinor, T. Rowe Price, Bill Gates

name: Fortera
tagline: Cement that absorbs its own emissions
what: Reengineers cement chemistry to cut carbon dioxide per tonne by roughly 60%, retrofitting into existing kilns rather than requiring new plants.
why: Cement is around 8% of global emissions and almost nobody in this cohort will touch it. Khosla will, which is roughly his entire investing thesis in one position.
other_backers: Khosla Ventures, Temasek, Wollemi Capital

name: Stardust Solutions
tagline: Commercial solar geoengineering
what: Developing proprietary particles for stratospheric aerosol injection — deliberately reflecting sunlight to cool the planet. Raised roughly $75M, the largest known round in the sector, and announced outdoor experiments beginning April 2026.
why: The most ethically contested entry on this entire board, and included for exactly that reason. Private capital is now funding unilateral planetary intervention with no governing treaty, and research funding for the field tripled in a year.
other_backers: Future Ventures, Exor, Attestor, Future Positive Capital
